plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU) to zero for capital preservation.
Sell high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU) to zero to reduce risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with conservative limits.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk significantly.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by cutting leveraged and high-beta positions, but also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to reduce overall portfolio risk.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to align with balanced risk tolerance.
Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Buy LMT at 4% to add a quality, defensive name from the scanner list.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure while reducing concentration.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around ~2.5%/month growth, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, offering a more stable growth profile than aggressive, with moderate drawdown potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to existing high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to increase growth potential.
Add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to amplify returns.
Buy LMT at 6% as a strong scanner setup to further stretch growth.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, which can lead to substantial drawdowns and daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to near zero.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces growth potential and high-beta exposure, prioritizing steady distributions. NAV can still fall in selloffs, and distributions are variable.
